q2.answer: In the bone of the gum, next to the front teeth. It is called the alveolar cleft.

q3.answer: The small tooth next to the front tooth (lateral incisor). About half of children with a cleft do not have it on the cleft side.

q4.answer: The graft gives the eye tooth bone to come down into. It needs bone to grow into.
q4.where: Sheet 1, The eye tooth and Why surgeons do the bone graft

q5.answer: About 8 to 11 years old. They pick the time by how far the teeth have grown, not by age.
q5.where: Sheet 1, When surgeons do the graft

q7.answer: New bone fills the gap and the gum has healed over it. The eye tooth is a little lower.
q7.where: Sheet 2, key message box and What has changed

q8.answer: With an X-ray at about 3 to 6 months. It shows how well the new bone has taken.

q9.answer: The hip can be sore for a while.

q10.answer: It has come down through the new bone and is in the row of teeth.

q11.answer: Fixed braces. Almost everyone who has this graft needs them.

q12.answer: Two plans. 1) Close the space: braces move the eye tooth into the gap and the dentist reshapes it. 2) Keep the space: a plate with a false tooth while growing, then later an implant or a bridge with one wing. The cleft team will talk with you about which suits you.
